control_tower.notes: 30 exceptions collected while the day simulator plays the scripted scenarios (rolled back), each narrated through the runtime: schema, evidence resolvable in FHIR, guards. The human accuracy rating (evals/control_tower/narrator/rating_sheet.md) is outside the runner.

deid_check.notes: Span-level recall and precision of the whole pipeline (rule layer + second pass); a case passes when nothing leaked and nothing was wrongly redacted.

feedback_classify.notes: 60 comments, 15 per language (EN, FR, ZH, PA), with star rating. Sentiment accuracy, exact theme-set match and micro-F1 over themes.

medication_reconciliation.notes: A case passes when every reconciliation row has the labelled discrepancy type.

mri_implant_extract.notes: Exact match of device categories per answer, across English, French, Chinese and Punjabi.

order_review.notes: A case passes when the flagged concern types equal the labels (no miss, no extra) with a valid, grounded commentary.

patient_message_triage.notes: Category and urgency (after the rule layer) of synthetic patient messages; cases from human review are appended by the low-confidence workflow.

policy_qa.notes: 16 answerable questions (expected policy cited with a verbatim quote) and 4 the documents do not cover (must say so). Citations are checked against the retrieved text by the server.

protocol_suggest.notes: Top-1 and top-3 hit rate over retrieval candidates from the synthetic protocol library.

referral_weekly_summary.notes: Weekly summary drafted for three synthetic data sets. Every number must be a fact filled in by the server; drafts with their own digits fail validation.

requisition_extract.notes: Field-level accuracy against generator labels. 30% of requisitions are free-text letters.

requisition_triage.notes: Agreement with the labelled priority (P1-P4). Under-triage is the safety-relevant error.

summary.what: WP3 day simulator: a full planned day (07:00 to 08:00 the next day) with and without the ICU surge scenario; no model involved

note: Mock model: a baseline that shows the pipeline (context, schema, guards, evidence), not a model's quality; mock costs are list-price estimates.
